mainTopic: How a shared הפרה works (cutting off a share or weakening the vow), and whether a חכם can undo a husband's הקמה or הפרה, including repeated and linked declarations
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a betrothed girl whose father and husband share the power to cancel her vow. If the father cancelled and the husband died before hearing, the father cancels only the husband's share. רבי נתן says that is the view of בית שמאי, while בית הלל say he cannot do it that way. From this the גמרא concludes that for בית שמאי one partner's הפרה cuts off his half (מיגז גייז), but for בית הלל it only weakens the whole vow (מקלש קליש). Then רבא asks whether a חכם can undo a husband's הקמה, and if so, whether he can undo a הפרה. רבי יוחנן answers that a הקמה can be undone but a הפרה cannot. רבה asks what happens if the husband said 'קיים ליכי' twice and only the first was undone. The answer, from a rule of רבא, is that the second one then takes effect. Finally רבה asks about a husband who upholds and cancels together and makes the הקמה depend on the הפרה. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The father cancels the dead husband's share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that if the father already cancelled his share and the husband died before hearing the vow, the father may now cancel the husband's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her father heard the vow and cancelled it, and the husband never got to hear it before he died, the father goes back and cancels the husband's part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא as evidence for its earlier question about how הפרה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed girl's vow needs both the father and the husband to cancel it. If the husband dies, his power passes back to the father. The ברייתא says the father only has to cancel the husband's part, because his own part was already cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: the husband's portion of the vow

phrases.english: If her father heard and nullified the vow for her,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק הַבַּעַל לִשְׁמוֹעַ עַד שֶׁמֵּת
phrases.english: and the husband did not manage to hear of it before he died,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹזֵר הָאָב וּמֵפֵר חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל.
phrases.english: the father goes back and nullifies the husband's portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted just before this passage to answer whether הפרה severs or weakens.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one partner's הפרה cuts off his half or only weakens the vow
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a father cancelling after the husband died

steps.title: רבי נתן: this ruling follows בית שמאי only
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the ruling above is the view of בית שמאי, but בית הלל say the father cannot cancel only the husband's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: That ruling is the opinion of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: he cannot cancel it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי נתן tells us the ruling is only בית שמאי's opinion, and that בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית הלל, cancelling only the husband's part is not enough. The father must cancel the whole vow again, including his own part. This מחלוקת is what the גמרא will use for its proof.

keyTerms.meaning: these are exactly the words of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: הֵן הֵן דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said: This is the statement of Beit Shammai.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין יָכוֹל לְהָפֵר.
phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: He cannot nullify.
phrases.notes: The father can't cancel just the husband's part. He has to cancel his own part again too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: הֵן הֵן דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling of step 1 a name (בית שמאי) and adds בית הלל's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the father cancels only the husband's share. בית הלל: he cannot do it that way.

steps.title: Proof: בית שמאי say 'severs,' בית הלל say 'weakens'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that for בית שמאי a הפרה cuts off one's half completely, while for בית הלל it only weakens the whole vow. The question is settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: according to בית שמאי, a הפרה cuts off his part. According to בית הלל, it only weakens the vow. Yes, learn this from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what the ברייתא proves and declares the earlier question answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father's first הפרה cut off his half completely, then only the husband's half is left, so he cancels just that, as בית שמאי say. בית הלל require him to redo the whole thing, so his first הפרה must have only weakened the vow overall. Since we follow בית הלל, הפרה weakens.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it / conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: one partner's הפרה cuts off (מיגז גייז) his own half. בית הלל, whom we follow: it only weakens (מקלש קליש) the whole vow, so the father must cancel all of it again.
steps.confusionAlert: The second שמע מינה is not a new proof. It just confirms that the question really is settled by this ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question the גמרא raised earlier about how a shared הפרה works.

phrases.english: Conclude from this:
according to Beit Shammai, it completely severs,
according to Beit Hillel, it only weakens.
Indeed, conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי מִיגָּז גָּיֵיז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא's מחלוקת in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to בית הלל, whom the הלכה follows, one partner's הפרה only weakens the vow and does not cut off his share.

steps.title: רבא asks: can a sage undo a confirmation or a cancellation?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a husband can go to a חכם to undo his הקמה of his wife's vow, and if he can, whether he can also undo a הפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Can one ask a חכם to undo a confirmation of a vow, or not? And if you say one can, can one ask to undo a cancellation, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רבא asks a two-part question about whether a חכם can undo a husband's decision about his wife's vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband who confirmed (הקים) a vow might regret it and want to cancel it after all. רבא asks whether a חכם can release him from his confirmation. Only if the answer is yes does he move on to ask whether a הפרה can also be undone, so the husband could confirm the vow instead.

keyTerms.meaning: asking a חכם to undo something
if you will say (introduces the second part of the question)

phrases.english: Rava asked: Is there a request to a sage regarding ratification,
phrases.notes: He means asking a חכם to undo the husband's confirmation of his wife's vow.

phrases.english: or is there no request regarding ratification?

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר יֵשׁ שְׁאֵלָה בְּהָקֵם:
phrases.english: If you say there is a request regarding ratification:
is there a request regarding nullification,
or is there no request regarding nullification?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Unrelated new question, starting a new section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a חכם undo a הקמה? If so, can he undo a הפרה?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a confirmation can be undone, a cancellation cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from רבי יוחנן: a חכם can undo a הקמה, but not a הפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבי יוחנן said: One may ask a חכם to undo a confirmation, but one may not ask to undo a cancellation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both parts of רבא's question with a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part one is answered yes: a הקמה can be undone by a חכם. Part two is answered no: once a husband cancels a vow, a חכם cannot bring it back.

keyTerms.meaning: one may ask (a חכם to undo)

steps.whatToRemember: A husband can ask a חכם to undo his הקמה, but a הפרה cannot be undone.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One may ask a sage to undo ratification,
but one may not ask to undo nullification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both parts of רבא's question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes to undoing a הקמה, no to undoing a הפרה.

steps.title: Two הקמות, and only the first is undone
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks: if the husband said 'קיים ליכי' twice and a חכם undid the first הקמה, does the second הקמה now take effect?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: If he said 'It is upheld for you, it is upheld for you,' and then asked a חכם about the first הקמה, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks a new question that builds on the last answer: a חכם can undo a הקמה. What if the husband said 'it is upheld' twice and only the first one was undone?
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he said 'קיים ליכי' the second time, the vow was already upheld, so maybe the second statement did nothing. If so, once the first is undone, the vow stands with no הקמה at all and he could still cancel it. Or maybe the second הקמה was waiting in the background and now takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question of law)
'It is upheld for you' — the words of a הקמה
He asked a חכם to undo it

phrases.english: Rabba asked:
"It is upheld for you, it is upheld for you,"
phrases.notes: The husband (or father) said this twice after hearing her vow.

phrases.english: and he asked a sage about the first upholding — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5's answer that a חכם can undo a הקמה, and applies it to a doubled הקמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the second הקמה, said while the vow was already upheld, takes effect once the first is undone.

steps.title: Answer from רבא: the second one takes effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבא's rule: if the first is undone by a חכם, the second takes effect. So the second הקמה now holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רבא said: If he asked a חכם about the first, the second takes effect on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה's question by quoting a rule of רבא. Once the first is undone, the second one kicks in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule shows that a repeated statement is not empty. It waits, and it takes effect as soon as the first one is removed. So the second 'קיים ליכי' upholds the vow, and the husband can no longer cancel it.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying something a second time is not wasted. If the first is undone, the second one takes effect.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rava said:
If he asked a sage about the first one —
the second one takes effect on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבה's question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Based on רבא's rule, once the first הקמה is undone, the second הקמה takes effect.

steps.title: Upheld and cancelled together, linked to each other
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks a new question: if he said 'it is upheld and it is cancelled,' and the הקמה takes effect only if the הפרה takes effect, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: If he said, 'It is upheld for you and it is cancelled for you, and the הקמה should not take effect unless the הפרה takes effect,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks a second, separate question, and the גמרא will discuss it next. Here the husband says both a הקמה and a הפרה at once and links them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually whichever comes first decides: if the vow is upheld, a later הפרה does nothing. Here he set a condition that the הקמה works only if the הפרה also works. The question is how these two can work together, since each one seems to block the other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is cancelled for you' — the words of a הפרה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new question, not part of the double-הקמה case. Here one הקמה and one הפרה are made to depend on each other.

phrases.english: Rabba asked:
"It is upheld for you, and it is cancelled for you,
and the upholding shall not take effect

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָלָה הֲפָרָה״, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: unless the cancelling takes effect" — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from the same אמורא, moving from two הקמות to a הקמה joined to a הפרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happens when a הקמה and a הפרה are said together and the הקמה is made to depend on the הפרה taking effect.
